inputs: The checkout itself: production and Company OS source, parsed but never imported or executed
Canonical bootstrap contracts, the capsule graph, and test-suite results the caller supplies
invariants: Unknown never satisfies a required condition; a required unknown blocks readiness exactly as a failure does.
There is no readiness score, health score or percentage; READY means every required check passed and nothing else.
A READY report does not authorize production integration; that stays a CEO decision (merge_major_architecture_rewrite).
The gate holds none of the authority it checks for: no network, no process spawn, no delete, no write outside a caller-named directory.
Every check is classified required or advisory in policy.py; an unclassified check fails the run rather than defaulting.
A blocker is resolved only with evidence; resolved=true without resolution_evidence is refused at construction.
Reports are append-only under a caller-supplied state directory and never overwritten with different content.
Nothing here is imported by another subsystem; this package reads Company OS and is read by none of it.
outputs: A canonical ProductionIntegrationReadinessReport: checks by category, blockers, unknowns, advisories
A deterministic READY, BLOCKED or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE verdict tied to a source commit and an as-of date
purpose: Evaluates deterministically whether Company OS is safe and complete enough to cross the production integration boundary, and reports what blocks it. It evaluates readiness; it never wires anything to production.
risks: A constant-path write scan cannot see a production path assembled at runtime; the no-network, no-spawn and no-delete conditions cover that case instead.
Suite results are supplied by the caller, so that condition is only as strong as the reporter named on the evidence.
The CEO dashboard depends on this capsule as its eventual readiness surface; no code coupling exists yet and the boundary checks prove it.
title: Production integration readiness gate
